issues.description: Field 'user_name' has inconsistent type expectations: the problem statement (problem_statement.md) explicitly instructs "Definieren Sie `user_name` als String-Buffer" but the solution (solution_repository/helloWorld.asm) declares 'user_name' as a 32-bit integer with the line 'user_name dd 0'. The template (template_repository/helloWorld.asm) does not provide a 'user_name' declaration. This mismatch will confuse students about the intended data representation (string buffer vs 32-bit integer) and may lead to incorrect declarations or misuse when passing 'user_name' to routines like printf that expect a pointer to a string.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the representation of 'user_name' consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution and template to declare 'user_name' as a string buffer to match the problem statement, for example: 'user_name: times 64 db 0' (or at minimum 'user_name db 0') and add the same declaration to template_repository/helloWorld.asm; or (B) if an integer was intended, update the problem statement text to specify that 'user_name' is a 32-bit value (dd) and adjust examples accordingly. Prefer option A if 'user_name' is meant to be passed to printf as a C-style string.
